instruction: Conduct a speed test on speedtest.net, export the full report with server details, and save it as ~/Network/SpeedTest/report.txt, creating directories as needed.

metadata.explanation: Task requires running a speed test on speedtest.net and exporting detailed results including server information. The evaluator uses a custom metric that validates the report file at ~/Network/SpeedTest/report.txt contains properly formatted speed test results with numeric values: Ping (with ms), Download (with Mbps/Kbps/Gbps), Upload (with Mbps/Kbps/Gbps), and Server information. This ensures the user completed the test and saved comprehensive, actual results rather than just keywords.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary scoring: 1.0 if the report contains properly formatted speed test results with regex-validated patterns (Ping with numeric value and ms, Download with numeric value and speed units, Upload with numeric value and speed units, Server with descriptive text) and has minimum content length (50 chars), 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all key instruction requirements: Ping, Download, Upload, and Server information
Robust regex-based validation prevents false positives by requiring numeric values with proper units (ms for Ping, Kbps/Mbps/Gbps for speeds)
Minimum content length check (50 chars) ensures detailed report, not just minimal text
Getter logic correctly reads file from specified path with proper encoding handling (UTF-8 with latin-1 fallback)
Binary scoring (1.0/0.0) is appropriate for this pass/fail verification task
All previously suggested fixes have been implemented: regex patterns, numeric validation, format validation, and content length check
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Directory creation is verified implicitly through file existence, but could add explicit directory structure check if needed
Minor: Server pattern '[a-zA-Z0-9]+' could be more strict to require minimum length, though single-char server names are unlikely in practice
